newsitem.title: GERMANY: Preussag shares off after says profits fall.
newsitem.headline: Preussag shares off after says profits fall.

text.p: Shares in German industrial group Preussag AG fell over three percent on Wednesday after the company said profits for the business year that ended on September 30 fell sharply from the previous year.
Preussag shares were down 13.50 marks at 360 marks, making it the worst performer out of the 30 leading stocks which make up the DAX index.
The rest of the market was firmer, with the DAX index up 14.22 points at 2,778.31 points by 1157 GMT.
Speaking to reporters in Dijon, France company chairman Michael Frenzel said results for the full year would correspond to the development in the first half, when profits plunged 30 percent.
But he said shareholders would still be offered an "attractive" dividend.
Management board members who asked not to be identified said the decline in after-tax profit would be in double-digits.

Frenzel, attributing the earnings decline to weakness in the steel industry, said group sales in 1995/96 slipped to 25.1 billion marks from 26.3 billion, largely because of a fall in steel sales at Preussag's trading unit.
